introBasis: your digital twin, Vision Pro and NEOM work, and the questions enterprise buyers ask before they fund an XR build
offerText: Your first article is on me.

cards.title: Digital Twin Projects Stall: Fix This Layer First
cards.angle: A September 2026 market analysis expects many announced enterprise twin initiatives to quietly stall by 2028, and a 2025 report found over 40% of manufacturers still in pilot. Diagnose data, simulation, interface, adoption and ownership separately.
cards.evidence: Your Microsoft project gave investors, officials and landowners an interactive view of a green hydrogen project's energy output with AI predictions. It was deployed during feasibility and fundraising and showcased at Microsoft's Co-Innovation Lab anniversary. It supported communication, which is not proof the whole twin program worked.
cards.formatNote: A diagnostic guide the buyer works through layer by layer.

cards.title: XR App Ownership: Your Exit Plan Checklist
cards.angle: Meta Spark, Adobe Aero, Wikitude, Vuforia Chalk and 8th Wall all shut down between Sept 2024 and March 2026, per one roundup. A procurement checklist should cover code, assets, licenses, build pipelines, device management and maintenance.
cards.evidence: Your site states clients get full IP and source code ownership, and your FAQ says Treeview has no outside investors. Tie the checklist to specific contract terms only if you can approve them.
cards.formatNote: One sharp claim about platform risk, backed by a list every buyer recognizes.

cards.title: WebXR or Native Headset App? Decide Here
cards.angle: The WebXR Device API reached W3C Candidate Recommendation status on June 9, 2026, but Safari and Firefox still lack support per one roundup. Compare reach, device features, performance, distribution, maintenance and security; neither model always wins.
cards.evidence: Your Microsoft twin shipped across HoloLens 2, mobile and WebGL, and your Treaty Story app is native on Apple Vision Pro. Both delivery models appear in your own work.
cards.formatNote: A buyer's decision guide comparing two delivery models across six factors.

cards.title: AR Wayfinding: Test Before You Deploy
cards.angle: Snap's $2,195 Specs and Android XR glasses both ship this fall, so mobility use cases are moving from headsets to glasses. Evaluate tracking, route mapping, usability and environment before committing, because a proof of concept isn't a deployment.
cards.evidence: Your NEOM work on Magic Leap 2 explored Trojena's ski village with a slalom route mapping tool, performance visualizers and session reports. Your page calls it a proof of concept assessing feasibility, not a deployed system.
cards.formatNote: One proof of concept and one hardware shift.

cards.title: Enterprise XR ROI: Read the Claims Carefully
cards.angle: A Meta-commissioned Forrester study reports 219% ROI on VR training, while a separate roundup finds only 7% of organizations use VR in training. Define the baseline, unit of measurement and counterfactual before trusting any benchmark.
cards.evidence: Your Microsoft twin page cites better stakeholder communication and support for feasibility decisions, and publishes no financial ROI figure. That gap is the point of the article.
cards.formatNote: One benchmark and one gap, written for the buyer who has to defend the budget.
